newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa mulls extending 96/97 maize export period.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa mulls extending 96/97 maize export period.

text.p: South Africa's Maize Advisory Committee on Thursday recommended that the deadline for application for export permits by private traders should be extended until April 30, 1997.
Previously permits for export were only valid until December 31, 1996.
The committee said in a statement the next date for export permit applications, for shipment during the months of February to April 1997, would be January 15.
According to this season's maize marketing scheme private traders, who made their debut in the export market in the 1996/97 marketing year, may export up to 1.8 million tonnes of maize.

A Maize Board spokeswoman told Reuters on Thursday permits for exports totalling 1.66 million tonnes had already been issued. This comprised permits for 711,883 tonnes of white maize, 761,205 tonnes of yellow and 188,000 tonnes of maize products.
